core_obligations: Define F as the Zariski sheafification of the Frobenius colimit functor and identify its sections on quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects (proof lines 11865-11873).
Check conditions (1) and (2) of the h sheaf criterion, the second through the fppf sheaf property of O and commutation of the colimit with equalizers (proof lines 11875-11884).
Check condition (3) by solving the algebra problem for a', a'' with F^n(a' - a'') in fA + J, including the uniqueness up to Frobenius replacement (proof lines 11886-11910).
Check condition (4) using the funny blowup lemma, where E = P^1_Z (proof lines 11912-11920).
proof_roadmap: Condition (3) as an algebra problem with uniqueness (proof lines 11886-11910).
Condition (4) via the funny blowup (proof lines 11912-11920).
difficulty_reason: For a prime p and a scheme S over F_p, the lemma states that on the big h site (Sch/S)_h there is a unique sheaf F with F(X) = colim_F Gamma(X, O_X) for every quasi-compact and quasi-separated object X, the colimit being along the Frobenius action (statement lines 11854-11863). The proof takes the Zariski sheafification of the functor X -> colim_F Gamma(X, O_X), notes that on quasi-compact and quasi-separated X the sections are unchanged by Sheaves, Lemma labelled sheaves-lemma-directed-colimits-sections, and reduces the sheaf property to conditions (1), (2), (3) and (4) of Lemma labelled lemma-refine-check-h (proof lines 11865-11877). Condition (1) is immediate from the sheafification; condition (2) is reduced to the fact that O is an fppf sheaf (Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-sheaf-condition-holds) together with the commutation of colim_F with equalizers of F_p-algebras (proof lines 11879-11884). Condition (3) is turned into an explicit algebra problem: given a', a'' with F^n(a' - a'') in fA + J one must produce a and m with a - F^m(a') in J and a - F^m(a'') in fA, uniquely up to the replacement (a, m) going to (F(a), m + 1), and the proof does this by writing F^n(a' - a'') = fh + g and taking a = F^n(a') - g with m = n, then proving uniqueness by showing a - a_1 is nilpotent and hence killed by a large power of F (proof lines 11886-11910). Condition (4) follows from Lemma labelled lemma-funny-blow-up and the fact that E = P^1_Z in that example (proof lines 11912-11920). Turning the two sheaf conditions into the concrete algebra problem with a uniqueness statement modulo Frobenius is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
